A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WEATHER-5K and PhysicsFormer. Their main text, Appendices A–E, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V3 reports original forecasting benchmarks, extreme-event scores, efficiency measurements, an input-length ablation, and heatwave case studies.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The pressure–wind loss changes from a shared learnable scalar alpha in v3 Equation 7 to station-specific alpha_i in v4 Equation 11. The Transformer residual architecture remains. The graph/neural-ODE discussion newly specifies the previously underspecified dynamic core without establishing that the core was replaced.

E1.justification: The global station dataset, five weather variables, and Chongqing heatwave scenarios remain. V4 Figure 3a introduces a London title, but its retained curves and the Chongqing station identification in Section 3.4 indicate a labeling inconsistency, not demonstrated additional geographical coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–3 and 8–9, including ECMWF-HRES and the appendix comparisons with WSSM, UniMTD, and UniTraj. Updated citations and publication years do not introduce evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 corrects the stated training start from 2013-01-01 to 2014-01-01 and the station count from 5,762 to 5,672, aligning with the existing main-text specification. These are reported-setting corrections; rerunning experiments is not established. Forecast horizons, input lengths, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The iTransformer input-length ablation retains lengths 24–120 and a fixed 72-step forecast horizon, moving from Figure 8 to Figure 9. Heatwave studies, dataset analyses, and forecast examples are retained. Moving the ERA5 comparison into the main text adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions state in Section 4.5 that results are reported once and assert stability across seeds. Neither adds run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Existing distribution statistics and heatwave variability bands are retained.

E6.justification: Matched forecasting scores, efficiency measurements, distribution statistics, and ablation outcomes remain unchanged in Tables 2–3 and 6–9 and the corresponding figures. PhysicsFormer’s average temperature MAE remains 2.34, and its heatwave MAE remains 1.23. The relocated ERA5 plots retain their results.

T1.justification: V4 Equations 3–5 add a weighted graph-gradient definition and neural-ODE evolution and integration equations for the existing dynamic core. The pressure–wind coefficient is also mathematically refined. This adds formal specification of one component; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.2, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: WEATHER-5K, operational benchmarking, extreme-event and efficiency evaluation, and PhysicsFormer. The claims about the forecasting gap between TSF and operational NWP retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 adds substantive explanations connecting irregular station geometry to graph derivatives and interpreting the dynamic core as a physical prior. The relocated heatwave discussion drops v3 Appendix D’s blanket assertion that ERA5 cannot accurately capture extreme events while retaining the station-specific underestimation finding.

D1.justification: V4 substantially expands documentation of the previously opaque dynamic core: Haversine nearest-neighbor graph construction, distance-weighted learned gradient projection, GNN tendencies, autoregressive integration, and a fourth-order Runge–Kutta solver. These details improve reproducibility of a key component, although the neighbor count and precise GNN configuration remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V4 replaces the Han et al. POI-recommendation STGCN citation with Yu et al.’s traffic-forecasting STGCN and adds Smith et al.’s ISD paper. The introduction distinguishes physics-based NWP from data-driven forecasting. Most other reference revisions update publication metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: Local copyediting throughout the main text and datasheet corrects grammar, redundancy, and terminology. Section 4.3 is expanded, existing ERA5 discussion moves into Section 3.4, affiliations and running headers change, and acknowledgements are added. The overall narrative and section sequence remain.

P2.justification: V3’s six-panel Figure 6 is divided between v4’s main-text Figure 3 and appendix Figure 7. The heatwave legend, radar normalization caption, and main-table wind labels are revised, with associated reflow and renumbering. The relocated heatwave panel introduces the inconsistent London heading.

improvement.justification: V4 makes the dynamic core substantially easier to understand and corrects inconsistent training dates, station counts, citations, and prose. These provide a limited overall quality gain while preserving the empirical evidence. The new London label on the Chongqing plot harms consistency, and missing graph/GNN settings still limit reproducibility, preventing a stronger improvement judgment.
